cards.anchor: Meet the synthetic three-elevation attenuation-spread target of at most 4 percent at second 120, with fewer stirring seconds where feasible.
cards.burden: Allocate two fresh trials to this card and four to the companion card, exhausting the six-trial session budget. Record every five-second check, stop decision, actual cessation time, duration and final reading. This single pair provides limited causal evidence.
cards.construction: Hypothesis: disconnecting optical failures from further agitation can preserve the sample target while reducing stirring. Compare nominal 900 rpm for exactly 60 seconds, logging the optical rule in shadow mode, against nominal 900 rpm controlled by three successive five-second checks at most 4 percent, capped at second 105. Precommit and record treatment order. Both use 150 mL water and 0.30 mL dye, fresh rinsed vessels, one dye bottle, fixed addition location and locked camera. Sample at second 120, withdrawing 1 mL at each specified depth within ten seconds; reverse sampling order across the pair. Use common-aliquot and water references, the spill tray, and stop if liquid escapes.
cards.defeat: A timer-trial spread above 4 percent defeats its bounded sufficiency in this pair. Useful-loop support also fails if the enabled rule stops by second 60 or consumes no more stirring. Both sample failures leave the comparison unresolved; even both passing with a duration difference cannot identify bubbles or isolate a disturbance mechanism.
cards.mutation: Replace the optical-to-stirring command link with a fixed timer while retaining the original rule as an observable shadow decision.
cards.prediction_candidate: If the proposed costly feedback dependency operates and 60 seconds suffices, both trials pass the final sample target while the enabled trial continues beyond second 60 and uses more stirring despite timer-trial shadow failures.
cards.prediction_rival: If unresolved gradients require additional mixing, the 60-second trial fails the sample target while a longer enabled trial passes. This favors additional mixing in this pair without proving the particular speed or rule necessary.
cards.probe: Compare raw final-vial spreads and total stirring seconds against the shadow and enabled decision traces. Continue images after cessation and record depression and speck-containing frames as descriptive evidence; do not infer speck identity. Report unequal quiet durations explicitly.
cards.rival: Actual concentration gradients cause optical spread and the additional agitation usefully redistributes dye.
unknowns: No matched 900 rpm sample evidence or actual duration saving is already observed.
Different quiet durations, sequential sampling disturbance, nominal speed and one pair limit attribution.
Specks are unidentified; reference repeatability is not concentration calibration.

cards.anchor: Achieve the same at-most-4-percent final three-depth sample proxy at second 120 while potentially eliminating powered stirring for this recipe.
cards.burden: Allocate four trials as two transfer-versus-300-rpm pairs, reversing treatment order in the second pair and depth-sampling order within each pair. Together with PC-C1 this uses six trials. Manual transfers require additional handling; record transfer start/end times and spills. There is no demonstrated labor or energy saving.
cards.construction: Hypothesis: deliberate low-to-high bulk transport can replace rotation. In transfer trials leave the stirrer off and use the needle-free 20 mL syringe for three complete low-position withdrawals and upper-side returns, initiated at seconds 10, 30 and 50 and completed by second 60. Each comparator commands 300 rpm for exactly 60 seconds without transfers. No optical-driven restart or further redistribution follows. Hold recipe, dye bottle, rinsing, addition location, camera and references fixed; use the spill tray and stop if liquid escapes. All trials have a common quiet interval from second 60 to 120, then the stipulated depth-vial sampling protocol. Record any incomplete or late transfer as a protocol failure.
cards.defeat: Any transfer trial above 4 percent defeats success for that trial; repeated transfer failures with passing rotation comparators oppose the substitution. If both treatments fail, the recipe session is unresolved. Passing transfers support only this bounded construction, not complete-volume homogeneity or general transfer sufficiency.
cards.mutation: Substitute three metered vertical bulk transfers for rotational mixing and remove side-image spread from operational control.
cards.prediction_candidate: If metered vertical redistribution suffices, both transfer trials meet the final sample target with zero powered stirring, even if their side-image checks are not consistently at most 4 percent. Fixed 300 rpm comparator success remains a hypothesis despite one stipulated precedent.
cards.prediction_rival: If the transfer path redistributes only part of the volume and leaves depth gradients, transfer trials exceed 4 percent while fixed 300 rpm comparators pass; order-sensitive readings would weaken either causal account.
cards.probe: Compare two paired raw depth-vial spreads, target failures, commanded stirring duration and completed transfer counts. Log side images every five seconds independently of control. Retain all readings and compare reversed sampling orders; do not treat quiet side images as proof of success.
cards.rival: Rotation supplies broader redistribution than three localized syringe returns, whose apparent success could instead reflect sampling disturbance.
unknowns: No successful transfer construction is observed; three transfers are an unverified dose.
Transfers and sampling can disturb gradients; two trials per treatment cannot establish reliability.
Absolute concentration and unsampled-volume homogeneity are unmeasured; other fluids, sizes and continuous processes remain untested.
